title: "Nginx: Reverse Proxy and Routing"
description: "A worked microservices lesson using one small shop example."

**Course source:** Day 3 §1.3. The running application contains Product, Order and User services.

## Start with the simplest working gateway

The course first teaches forward versus reverse proxy, then uses Nginx routes to send requests to Order and Product. A **reverse proxy** receives a client request and forwards it to a backend chosen by server-side configuration. The client does not need to know the backend address.

For our shop, an illustrative Nginx config is:

~~~nginx
server {
    listen 8080;
    location /api/products/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:4101/products/;
    }
    location /api/orders {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:4103/orders;
    }
}
~~~

The trailing slashes and URI part of `proxy_pass` affect how Nginx rewrites paths. Test the actual forwarded URI; a small mismatch can produce a backend 404.

## Proxy is not gateway business logic

Nginx handles efficient HTTP termination, path routing and proxy-related controls. A sophisticated gateway may additionally understand business-specific policies or integrate with identity and discovery systems.

~~~text
Client: /api/products/7
Nginx:  /products/7  -> Product
~~~

In the Node lab, a tiny HTTP server performs a similar rewrite without Nginx.

## Timeouts must fit the budget

Nginx, Order and Product each may have separate deadlines. If the gateway waits 1.2 seconds but Order gives Product 350 milliseconds, Order may fail first. A too-short edge deadline can abort otherwise successful requests; an unlimited one permits resource accumulation.

## Operational test

Call the Product endpoint directly and through the reverse proxy. Verify status, headers, path, payload, latency and whether the selected instance is healthy.

Use Nginx when you need standard reverse proxy capabilities; use a richer API gateway only when its additional policies justify the cost.

[Nginx proxy documentation](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html).

## Check your understanding

Explain the request or event path end to end. Which component can fail, and which information would you collect to diagnose that failure?

## Mathematical Abstraction

Reverse-proxy rewriting transforms a public request path into an upstream path.

$$
\rho:\mathrm{/api/products/}x\mapsto\mathrm{/products/}x
$$

$x$ is the remaining path suffix. Exact URI rewriting depends on proxy configuration and trailing-slash semantics.
